findings_new.title: Defensive cross-check only guards review=None — a stale DIRTY review from a prior attempt can still beat a clean stamp on a re-judge
findings_new.detail: The cross-check (passed AND violation_count==0) lives INSIDE 'if review is None:'. The gate loop never clears STATE_VERIFICATION_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW between attempts (only JUDGE_META is popped in finally). So in a multi-attempt gate where a prior dirty attempt left a dirty review in the slot AND the final clean attempt's output_key write is lost to a state-prop failure while its stamp lands, finalize reads the stale dirty review (non-None) -> skips the cross-check -> fail-closes on stale data, dropping the clean verdict (the #172 harm, residual multi-attempt case). Code-structure gap confirmed by 2 independent lenses; whether the 'stamp lands but output_key lost' window is reachable is unverified (both ride the same child->parent state merge). Pre-existing since r1 (r2 only added violation_count to the condition; did not touch the review=None gating). All three load-bearing invariants still hold.
findings_new.recommended_fix: Cheap + closes the gap: clear the review slot before each re-judge so a lost final write yields None and hits the existing cross-check; OR extend the cross-check to a parseable-but-dirty review whose stamp records a later clean attempt (attempt mismatch).

findings_new.title: STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT absent from state_init._COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_KEYS entry-clearing — a reused InMemory session can carry a prior invocation's clean stamp
findings_new.detail: state_init clears _COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_KEYS (VERIFICATION/FINAL review + repair keys + JUDGE_META) to '' at pipeline entry so 'a stale review from a previous invocation must never be read as this run's verdict' — but the new stamp key is NOT in that list. Extends r1 note #2. Production (Vertex/Database) is safe: ADK trims temp: keys from persisted deltas. InMemorySessionService (tests/dev) reuses the session dict, so a prior invocation's clean stamp could survive and satisfy a new run's cross-check if that run's judge produces nothing AND its callback does not re-stamp.
findings_new.recommended_fix: Add STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT to _COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_KEYS in state_init.py (and optionally pop it in the gate finally blocks alongside JUDGE_META).

findings_new.title: Stamp's 'parseable' field is write-only dead state; the prop-failure warning hardcodes review_parseable=False though the triggering stamp always has parseable=True
findings_new.location: tenant_scorer/callbacks/compliance_enforcement.py:164 (write); guards boundary_compliance_remediation.py:334-338 + final_compliance_remediation.py:280-284 (read only passed/violation_count); warning extra boundary:339-346 + final:285-292
findings_new.detail: Grep confirms no get('parseable') reader of the stamp in tenant_scorer/; both guards consume only passed/violation_count/judge_kind. passed=True is only ever stamped with parseable=True (_emit_review_telemetry), so every firing of the clean_verdict_state_prop_failure warning concerns a parseable verdict, yet the warning logs review_parseable=False (hardcoded) — conflating 'slot missing at finalize' with 'judge output unparseable' in the BQ/Sentry contract.
findings_new.recommended_fix: Drop 'parseable' from the stamp (+ its test assertions), or log the stamp's actual value: 'review_parseable': verdict.get('parseable').

findings_new.title: r1 imprecise ctx.state comment re-asserted in NEW r2 comment lines ('snapshot taken at construction' — ADK wraps session.state by reference)
findings_new.detail: ADK 2.2.0 Context.__init__ sets self._state = State(value=session.state, ...) — the SAME dict by reference, not a copy. The None-read divergence arises only when the session service REASSIGNS session.state mid-run. The new r2 comments repeat the r1-flagged imprecise 'snapshot taken at construction' wording and could mislead future maintainers about when ctx.state goes stale.
findings_new.recommended_fix: Reword to: 'ctx.state._value references the session.state dict captured at construction; if the session service reassigns session.state during a child run_node, that reference goes stale while ctx.session.state re-reads the live attribute.'

The dirty-stamp path runs the same fall-through branch as the tested no-stamp case, so risk is low — but the explicit dirty-stamp assertion is unpinned for the final gate.
findings_new.recommended_fix: Mirror the boundary classes: add test_dirty_stamp_does_not_prevent_abort to TestFinalGateDefensiveCrossCheck and test_none_review_with_dirty_stamp_fail_closes to TestFinalizeFinalGateCrossCheck with judge_kind 'final'.
